clue.text: Resentment as nightclub (northern) gets temporary accommodation

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a nightclub up north is being turned into a temporary lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is a feeling of dissatisfaction or grievance, a close synonym of resentment.

clue.text: Bishop takes part in protests and quits services

indicators.note: the bishop letter joins in, going inside the protests

parts.note: demos are demonstrations
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric joins demonstrations and leaves the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: To demob is to discharge from the forces, so 'demobs' fits as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob, short for demobilise, is to release from military service, so it matches leaving the forces.

clue.text: Tricks to astonish brother's middle son

parts.note: to stun is to astonish

indicators.note: middle takes the central letter of brother

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Pranks meant to amaze a family's middle child.
explanation.walkthrough: Brother has seven letters, so its middle one is the fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunts are daring or showy feats, a synonym of tricks performed to impress.

clue.text: Mapmakers in UN censor ad: very unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of UN censor ad very are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A United Nations censor finds an advertisement highly odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ordnance Survey is the UK government body producing official maps, a mapping agency.

clue.text: Old artist's getting in bath regularly with island folk!

indicators.note: the bath letters get in to the artist's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter; with 's

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of bath, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: An Old Master takes a bath alongside Pacific islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was a 16th-century Venetian painter; it was Gauguin who famously painted Tahitians, which adds to the surface's charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahitians are the people of Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Person who puts labels on prepared ramen

indicators.note: prepared suggests the ramen letters are made up into something new

explanation.surface: Someone sticks labels on packets of ready-made noodles.
explanation.definitionFit: A namer is one who gives names, i.e. assigns labels to things.

clue.text: Rugby player runs into dad

indicators.note: the runs letter is placed into the word for dad

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rugby forward charges into his father.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in a rugby scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union a prop is one of the two front-row forwards in the scrum, an example of a player position.

clue.text: What one may suffer from if one gets very nosey?

definitions.text: What one may suffer from if one gets very nosey?

parts.words: What one may suffer from if one gets very nosey?
parts.note: nosey usually means prying, but read literally as having a troublesome nose it points to a nasal ailment

explanation.walkthrough: 'nosey' pretends to mean inquisitive; taken literally, a very nosey person has trouble in the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is inflammation of the nasal lining, from Greek rhis, meaning nose.

clue.text: Send message to workers making spectacles

parts.note: to page someone is to send them a message by pager
worker ants, so ants are workers

explanation.surface: Messaging the staff about making glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' looks like eyeglasses but means grand shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageants are elaborate public shows or processions, i.e. spectacles in the sense of displays.

clue.text: Country where wife-swapping is rife? It's the way things stand

definitions.meaning: cryptic sense: a nation full of love affairs

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, a state (country) of affairs (liaisons); the second is its everyday meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of affairs is the current situation or set of circumstances.

clue.text: Hill hiding ammo underneath? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: the clue claims the hill hides the ammo, signalling a concealed word
reverses the claim: it is the words 'ammo underneath' that conceal the hill, not the hill hiding ammo

explanation.surface: A hill with ammunition buried beneath it, then a twist that turns the idea around.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as a hill concealing ammo, then flip it: 'ammo underneath' conceals the hill, in amMO UNDerneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound is a small raised heap of earth, essentially a little hill.

clue.text: Actors going to SE town to get hamper

parts.note: hams are actors who overact
Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, in south-east England

explanation.surface: Performers travel to a south-eastern town to collect a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a basket but is the verb to hinder; Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or thwart them, a figurative synonym for hinder or impede.

clue.text: Minor role in two pieces?

parts.note: a bit and a part are both pieces, so a small role is literally two pieces

explanation.walkthrough: Both words of the phrase mean a piece, so a minor role read literally is made of two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small acting role with few lines, a minor part in a play or film.

clue.text: Drink found in garrets in Athens

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words garrets in Athens

explanation.surface: A drink is discovered in attic rooms in the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in garRETS IN Athens, and Athens fits the surface because the drink is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Go "eco" in salt? Strangely, there's nothing in it for this scientist

indicators.note: in it says the nothing letter goes inside the rearranged letters
strangely signals the letters of go eco in salt are put in an odd new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A green slogan sprinkled in salt water, puzzling an ocean scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: The scare quotes around eco make it look like a slogan, but it is just fodder; the salt hints at the sea the scientist studies.
explanation.definitionFit: An oceanologist studies the seas, a kind of scientist; the clue's sea salt hints at the field.

clue.text: Where is to rent, apart from that?

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, torn apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Asking where a property is for hire, and what else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like letting a property but is the past tense of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise can mean 'in other respects' or 'except for that', as in a phrase like 'otherwise fine'.

clue.text: Perfect kind of order for dessert

explanation.walkthrough: 'apple-pie order' is an idiom for something perfectly tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a baked fruit pudding and also an idiom for impeccable neatness.

clue.text: Bet against glutton being prickly type?

parts.note: to hedge is to bet on the other side to limit losses
a pig is a greedy eater

explanation.surface: A gambler hedges against a greedy, tetchy character.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedgepig is an old dialect name for the hedgehog.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgepig is a hedgehog, an animal covered in spines, hence a prickly creature.

clue.text: Tries to influence a school boss: keeps at it

parts.note: to press someone is to urge or try to persuade them
a head is a headteacher, the boss of a school

explanation.surface: A parent lobbies the headteacher, refusing to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To press ahead is to continue determinedly despite difficulty, an idiom meaning persevere.

clue.text: Rabbit that might be served for breakfast

definitions.meaning: to rabbit on is to talk at length

definitions.text: that might be served for breakfast
definitions.meaning: a griddled batter cake eaten at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for chatter (rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk), not the animal on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Waffle means rambling talk, a synonym of rabbiting on, and also a crisp batter cake.

clue.text: Bit of a nerve, getting news about currency

indicators.note: the news letters go about, around, the currency

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, so news (plural) is two Ns
the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: Someone has the cheek to report on money matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Treating news as the plural of new, a pair of the new abbreviation, is a crossword liberty worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, a single component of the nervous system.

clue.text: Head of Romans seized by military unit — held in this?

indicators.note: the letter is captured inside the military unit

parts.note: a legion is a Roman army unit

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Romans

explanation.surface: A Roman captive is grabbed by soldiers and shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: a prisoner seized by a legion might be held in this.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a shackle fastened round the ankle, a fetter in which a prisoner is held.

clue.text: Girl I sob over

indicators.note: over signals the word for sob is turned back to front

parts.note: to moan is to wail, like sob

explanation.surface: A young woman weeps over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Increase in spending as match official delayed

parts.note: ref is short for referee
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Spending goes up because the referee was held up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflate an economy is to stimulate it by boosting the money supply or government expenditure.

clue.text: Go with Italian lager and spicy sausage

parts.note: go and pep both mean energy or vigour
Peroni is a well-known Italian brand of beer

explanation.surface: Order Italian beer to accompany a spicy salami.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a dry, peppery Italian-American salami, an example of a seasoned sausage.

clue.text: Deduce friend not quite crazy

indicators.note: crazy signals the remaining letters are jumbled
not quite means the word friend loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Concluding that a pal is a bit unhinged, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims friend to FRIEN, and 'crazy' shuffles those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Therefore, monster returns

indicators.note: returns means the monster word is read backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a monster

explanation.surface: So the monster is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for 'consequently', used in English to mean hence.

clue.text: Director: genius embracing beginnings of silent era

indicators.note: the genius wraps around the two first letters

parts.note: Einstein's name is used to mean a genius

indicators.note: beginnings of takes the first letters of silent and era

explanation.surface: A film director of the silent era is hailed as a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: Sergei Eisenstein directed Battleship Potemkin in the silent era, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was a pioneering Soviet film-maker, an example of a director.
